Hi Priyom,

We started seeing a sustained spike of 5xx responses and token-queueing on our dedicated pool at ~08:30 PT. Latency for the /v1/generate route has climbed from ~120ms p90 to ~900ms p90 and a subset of requests are returning 500/502. Our payments flows are impacted (retries piling on).

Attached are: a short CSV of the request-level traces and one screenshot of the 5xx errors from our side.

This is on our reserved capacity (contract D-8271). We need a plan in the next 60 minutes — can you confirm whether this is a headroom/oversubscription issue with your dedicated GPUs or a serving regression on a model variant? We have a high-visibility trading window and will have revenue impact if this continues.

Thanks,
Sally Chen

Subject: Re: production errors this morning - AlphaPay

Quick technical readout for the group (initial):

What we see:
- Dedicated GPU pool for AlphaPay hit sustained queue depth increase at 08:27 PT. Token-processing latency rose and continuous batching rules pushed some requests into larger micro-batches leading to tail latency spikes.
- We observed a subset of model worker processes reporting transient OOMs/restarts for the quantized L2 model variant (l2-q4) between 08:30–08:35. Those restarts produce 502s until the worker recovers.
- Headroom metrics: reserved capacity was at ~92% utilization at peak; normal expected headroom is ~75–80% for this contract.

Immediate mitigations executed (09:30 PT):
1) Increased eviction aggressiveness for KV caches to free memory on hot workers.
2) Temporarily disabled large micro-batch consolidation for routes pinned to l2-q4.
3) Drained and rotated 2 workers on the AlphaPay pool (restarted with conservative memory flags).

Next asks for AlphaPay ops:
- If possible, can you throttle non-critical background traffic / analytics traffic for the next 2 hours? That will reduce queue pressure while we monitor.

Plan: if headroom stays >90% for more than one more hour we will propose (A) a short-term burst authorization to dedicated spare capacity, or (B) a scheduled slot increase on your reserved pool. Estimate for a 2-hour burst: approx $4.2k. Will confirm exact numbers in the ops deck.

I'll keep the bridge open and post updates.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production errors this morning - AlphaPay

Thanks everyone for the fast work over the weekend — wanted to close the loop from the account / leadership side.

Summary and ask:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of (1) unusual traffic spike from a scheduled reconciliation job on AlphaPay's side and (2) a memory regression exposed in the l2-q4 runtime under that traffic pattern. The SRE mitigations prevented continued 5xx after 09:45 PT on 6/15.
- We have two paths:
  * Short term: authorize a bounded burst (we can provide a credit estimate) to restore capacity for the remainder of AlphaPay's high window. This avoids immediate customer-facing throttles.
  * Medium term: schedule a reserved slot increase + a post-mortem with engineering to harden l2-q4 for reconciliation-like workloads.

Action items:
1) AlphaPay ops: confirm whether you can suppress/schedule the reconciliation run outside of the next high-window.
2) Priyom: I need an approval-for-burst ask to finance for the ~$4.2k estimate or confirmation that we route this as billable.
3) Vivek / Naomi: please prepare a short post-mortem and a candidate patch for the quantized runtime by EOD Wednesday (6/18).

Sally, please confirm which path you prefer. We will keep priority support on the bridge until you sign off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
